verses: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ
إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ
لَّا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلَإِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ ٱلْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُۥ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ
فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُم مِّن طِينٍ لَّازِبٍۭ
وَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
فَإِنَّمَا هِىَ زَجْرَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ فَإِذَا هُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
هَٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
ٱحْشُرُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ وَأَزْوَٰجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْبُدُونَ
مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ
وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا عَلَيْكُم مِّن سُلْطَٰنٍۭ بَلْ كُنتُمْ قَوْمًا طَٰغِينَ
فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوٓا۟ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ
وَيَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَتَارِكُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتِنَا لِشَاعِرٍ مَّجْنُونٍۭ
وَمَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
لَا فِيهَا غَوْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ
قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّى كَانَ لِى قَرِينٌ
أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ
وَلَوْلَا نِعْمَةُ رَبِّى لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
أَذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُّزُلًا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِىٓ أَصْلِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
فَإِنَّهُمْ لَءَاكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِـُٔونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ
ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْبًا مِّنْ حَمِيمٍ
إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِهِمْ فَقَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
قَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ لَهُۥ بُنْيَٰنًا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
وَقَالَ إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌ
لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
أَمْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ إِنَٰثًا وَهُمْ شَٰهِدُونَ
وَجَعَلُوا۟ بَيْنَهُۥ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَبًا وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ ٱلْجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ
وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلَّا لَهُۥ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ
لَوْ أَنَّ عِندَنَا ذِكْرًا مِّنَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
فَإِذَا نَزَلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ فَسَآءَ صَبَاحُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ

leads.title: Abraham smashes the idols
leads.summary: In Genesis Rabbah, Abraham smashes the idols in his father's shop, blames the largest one, and is thrown into a furnace by Nimrod. In the Quran, Abraham breaks the idols except the biggest, tells the people to ask them, and is thrown into a fire made cool.

Shared motifs, rarest first: A substitute (animal or person) is given to the deity in place of a human life [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Prayer and substitute ritual for the recovery of Gaššuliyawiya, addressed to Lelwani (CTH 380.1): The deity is invited to eat the fat of the sacrificial animals, eat its fill, drink the blood and quench its thirst; A queen who saw a goddess in a dream failed to give her an offering, and later her illness is traced to it by oracle; A richly dressed woman (or animal) is sent to the angry deity as substitute for the sick person: better, pure, shining and white; Whether the deity eats the offered flesh, or the offerers and the poor do [response between the texts]; The king inquires of the gods by oracle and the oracle establishes the hidden cause of the plague; The supplicant vows that, if helped, he will proclaim the deity's praise (dalīlī ludlul).

Only in Abraham's dream and the near-sacrifice of his son: God ransomed the son with a great sacrifice (dhibh 'azim); When both had submitted he laid him on his forehead (talla-hu li-l-jabin); The father sees in a dream that he is sacrificing his son; The son of the sacrifice is not named; Isaac's birth is announced only after the episode (read as Ishmael by many exegetes); An angel calls from heaven to stop the sacrifice at the last moment; Father binds his son on the altar and lifts the knife; God commands a father to sacrifice his son; God commands a father to sacrifice his son [divergence between the texts]; The father lays the son down for the sacrifice [divergence between the texts]; Who the son to be sacrificed is and how he is named [divergence between the texts]; Lot believes in Abraham, who declares 'I am emigrating to my Lord'; A ram caught in a thicket is sacrificed in place of the son; and 11 more.

leads.title: Contest on Mount Carmel ↔ Moses and Aaron; Elias against Ba'l
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A single prophet of YHWH stands against 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah (weight 7.7); A prophet challenges the people who worship Baal [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); How the people respond to the prophet's challenge over Baal [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 23.2.

Only in Contest on Mount Carmel: Prophet repairs the ruined altar with twelve stones for the tribes of Jacob; Contest of gods: the god who answers by fire on an unlit sacrifice is God; The prophets of Baal are seized and slaughtered at the brook Kishon; Prophet mocks the silent god: perhaps he is musing, relieving himself, travelling, or asleep and must be woken; Sacrifice and altar drenched with four jars of water three times, filling a trench, before the miracle; The people fall on their faces crying 'YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!'; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; An offering consumed by fire as proof of the true God or messenger [response between the texts]; Fire from heaven falls and consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust and water; 'How long will you hop between two branches? If YHWH is God, follow him; if Baal, follow him'; Parable: a slave owned by quarreling partners versus a slave belonging wholly to one man; Prophets of Baal limp-dance around the altar and gash themselves with swords and lances till blood flows; and 8 more.

Only in Moses and Aaron; Elias against Ba'l: The prophet's name appears in variant form ('Il Yasin') for rhyme; Elias (Ilyas) rebukes his people: 'Will you call on Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?'; Aaron's standing before God [divergence between the texts]; Who is named as saved and credited at the deliverance from Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Refrain 'We left for him among later generations: Peace upon X... thus we reward those who do good'; Israel serves the Baals and the Ashtaroth/Asherahs; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Micaiah son of Imlah and the lying spirit: Prophet imprisoned on short rations of bread and water until the king returns in peace; God asks the heavenly council 'who will entice the king?'; a spirit volunteers; Four hundred court prophets unanimously promise victory; Prophet stakes his authority: 'If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me'; Court prophet makes iron horns: 'with these you will gore Aram'; A single true prophet, hated by the king because he never prophesies good for him; Prophet first sarcastically repeats the favorable oracle, then under oath tells the true one; A false prophet strikes the true prophet on the cheek; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [divergence between the texts]; Prophet sees God seated on his throne with all the host of heaven standing to his right and left; God uses a false prophet to test whether Israel loves him; A spirit volunteers in the divine council to be a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths; and 1 more.

Only in Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter: The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses; The arrogant king boasts of climbing the heights of Lebanon and cutting its cedars, drying up rivers with his feet; Proverb of crisis: children have come to the birth-stool and there is no strength to deliver; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant [divergence between the texts]; God says the conqueror's victories were planned by him long ago; the conqueror is only his instrument; The king tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and goes into the temple in crisis; Royal parricides flee to the land of Ararat; The escaped remnant shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward; a remnant goes out from Zion; God puts a spirit in the invader so that he hears a rumor and returns home; King spreads the enemy's threatening letter before God in the temple; Sign: this year eat aftergrowth, next year what springs of itself, the third year sow and reap; The 'virgin daughter of Zion' laughs at and wags her head after the enemy; and 9 more.

Only in Daughters of God denied; the angels' stations; closing doxology: Idolaters claim a kinship (nasab) between God and the jinn; the jinn know they will be brought to judgment; The angels say: each of us has a known station; we are ranged in ranks; we glorify; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; Whether the divine attendants (heralds [divergence between the texts]; A closing doxology and the divine title it uses [divergence between the texts]; Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts]; Polemic against assigning daughters to God (the angels as females) while preferring sons for themselves; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly.

leads.finding: God tests the patriarch's obedience

units.title: The binding of Isaac (Aqedah)

matches.label: God tests the patriarch's obedience
matches.note: Placement of the 'test'. Gen opens with it, wə-hā-ʾĕlōhîm nissâ ʾeṯ-ʾaḇrāhām, so the reader knows from the start that it is a trial. Q names it only after the rescue: inna hādhā la-huwa l-balāʾu l-mubīn. Gen's closing reason, kî ʿattâ yāḏaʿtî kî-yərēʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾattâ (now I know, 22:12), has no counterpart: in Q God does not come to know.

passages.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְהָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים נִסָּ֖ה אֶת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי
إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ

matches.label: God commands a father to sacrifice his son
matches.note: How the command comes. Gen: direct divine speech, qaḥ-nāʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā ... wə-lek-ləḵā ʾel-ʾereṣ ha-mmōriyyâ wə-haʿălēhû šām lə-ʿōlâ (a burnt offering at a named place). Q: a dream reported by the father, innī arā fī l-manāmi annī adhbaḥuka (I see in sleep that I slaughter you), with no place, no mountain and no ʿōlâ. Q's dhabaḥa is cognate with Hebrew zāḇaḥ, while Gen uses ʿōlâ and liš-ḥōṭ (22:10).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח נָ֠א אֶת בִּנְךָ֨ אֶת יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר אָהַ֨בְתָּ֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ לְךָ֔ אֶל אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: Who the son to be sacrificed is and how he is named
matches.note: Who the son is. Gen names him three times over: ʾeṯ-binḵā ʾeṯ-yəḥîḏəḵā ʾăšer-ʾāhaḇtā ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq. Q has only bi-ghulāmin ḥalīm (a forbearing boy) and announces Isaac only after the episode, wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn (37:112). This leaves the victim unnamed, and many exegetes read him as Ishmael. The 'only' (yāḥîḏ) son of Gen is not said.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח נָ֠א אֶת בִּנְךָ֨ אֶת יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר אָהַ֨בְתָּ֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ לְךָ֔ אֶל אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ
فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ
وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

matches.label: What the son to be sacrificed knows and says
matches.note: Who speaks, and what the son knows. Gen: Isaac does not know. He asks hinnēh hā-ʾēš wə-hā-ʿēṣîm wə-ʾayyēh ha-śśeh lə-ʿōlâ, and Abraham gives the veiled answer ʾĕlōhîm yirʾeh-lô ha-śśeh ... bənî. Q: the father tells him openly and asks his view, fa-nẓur mādhā tarā, and the son consents, yā-abati fʿal mā tuʾmaru sa-tajidunī in shāʾa llāhu mina ṣ-ṣābirīn. The address pair ʾāḇî / bənî matches yā-abati / yā-bunayya. Isaac's silence becomes the son's active submission.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִצְחָ֜ק אֶל אַבְרָהָ֤ם אָבִיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֔י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֶּ֣נִּֽי בְנִ֑י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְהָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאַיֵּ֥ה הַשֶּׂ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֱלֹהִ֞ים יִרְאֶה לּ֥וֹ הַשֶּׂ֛ה לְעֹלָ֖ה בְּנִ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

matches.label: The father lays the son down for the sacrifice
matches.note: The act. Gen: wood laid on Isaac, fire and knife, an altar built, wa-yyaʿăqōḏ ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq bənô wa-yyāśem ʾōṯô ʿal-ha-mmizbēaḥ mi-mmaʿal lā-ʿēṣîm, knife raised. Q: fa-lammā aslamā wa-tallahu li-l-jabīn, both 'submitted' and he laid him on his brow. No binding (ʿăqēḏâ), no altar, no wood, no fire and no three-day journey. The decisive word is the dual aslamā (both of them submitted).

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת עֲצֵ֣י הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיָּ֨שֶׂם֙ עַל יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת הָאֵ֖שׁ וְאֶת הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו

וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶֽל הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ וַיִּ֨בֶן שָׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת הָעֵצִ֑ים וַֽיַּעֲקֹד֙ אֶת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֹתוֹ֙ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ מִמַּ֖עַל לָעֵצִֽים
וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת יָד֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת לִשְׁחֹ֖ט אֶת בְּנֽוֹ
فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ

matches.label: Who stops the sacrifice of the son, and why
matches.note: Who stops it, and why. Gen: wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlâw malʾaḵ YHWH min-ha-ššāmayim ... ʾaḇrāhām ʾaḇrāhām wa-yyōʾmer hinnēnî; ʾal-tišlaḥ yāḏəḵā ʾel-ha-nnaʿar, because Abraham fears God. Q: wa-nādaynāhu an yā-Ibrāhīmu qad ṣaddaqta r-ruʾyā. God calls in the first person plural, with no angel and no hinnēnî. The reason is that Abraham has already fulfilled the dream, not a prohibition.

passages.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ מִן הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל תִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר וְאַל תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָּה כִּ֣י עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי יְרֵ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אַ֔תָּה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֛כְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת יְחִידְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽנִּי
وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

matches.label: What is offered in place of the son, and who provides it
matches.note: The substitute. Gen: Abraham looks up, sees ʾayil ʾaḥar neʾĕḥaz ba-ssəḇaḵ bə-qarnâw, and offers it ʿōlâ taḥaṯ bənô; he then names the place YHWH yirʾeh. Q: wa-fadaynāhu bi-dhibḥin ʿaẓīm. God himself ransoms (fadā) with a 'great sacrifice', the animal is unnamed, Abraham does not find it, and there is no place-name or temple-mount aetiology.

וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַבְרָהָ֛ם שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יְהוָ֣ה יִרְאֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵאָמֵ֣ר הַיּ֔וֹם בְּהַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרָאֶֽה

matches.label: The reward and blessing after the averted sacrifice
matches.note: The reward. Gen: bî nišbaʿtî nəʾum-YHWH ... bārēḵ ʾăḇāreḵḵā wə-harbâ ʾarbeh ʾeṯ-zarʿăḵā ... wə-yiraš zarʿăḵā ʾēṯ šaʿar ʾōyəḇâw wə-hiṯbārăḵû ḇə-zarʿăḵā kōl gôyê hā-ʾāreṣ, an oath and the unconditional blessing of the seed. Q: salāmun ʿalā Ibrāhīm ... wa-bāraknā ʿalayhi wa-ʿalā Isḥāqa wa-min dhurriyyatihimā muḥsinun wa-ẓālimun li-nafsihi mubīn. There is no oath and no conquest of enemy gates, and the offspring are explicitly mixed, some doing good and some wronging themselves.

leads.title: The Flood (full read) ↔ Noah called and was answered
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether and how Noah speaks to God [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God made Noah's descendants the only survivors (weight 7.7); Hero singled out as righteous or pious (weight 6.2). Pair score 21.7.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; and 43 more.

Only in Noah called and was answered: Noah called to God and God answered, saving him and his family from the great distress; How the story of Noah ends [divergence between the texts]; Three sons of the flood hero repopulate the whole earth; Refrain 'We left for him among later generations: Peace upon X... thus we reward those who do good'; After the flood the seed of mankind is preserved and humanity rises again; The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives.

units.title: The Flood (full read)

matches.label: Whether and how Noah speaks to God
matches.note: Who speaks first. In Genesis Noah never addresses God: God speaks (wa-yyōʾmer ʾĕlōhîm lə-nōaḥ, 6:13; wa-yyōʾmer YHWH lə-nōaḥ bōʾ-ʾattâ, 7:1), and God 'remembers' him (wa-yyizkōr ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-nōaḥ, 8:1). In Q 37:75 Noah takes the initiative and God answers: wa-la-qad nādānā Nūḥun fa-la-niʿma l-mujībūn, wa-najjaynāhu wa-ahlahu mina l-karbi l-ʿaẓīm. The silent righteous man becomes a praying prophet.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת כָּל הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֨וּחַ֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם
وَلَقَدْ نَادَىٰنَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ

leads.title: Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim ↔ Daughters of God denied; the angels' stations; closing doxology
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.8). Pair score 6.8.

Only in Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim: Those called God's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him [response between the texts]; God limits human lifespan to 120 years; Maidens of restrained glance whom no man or jinn has touched before them, like rubies and coral; Divine beings take human women as wives; Giants or heroes (Nephilim) born from divine-human unions.

Only in Daughters of God denied; the angels' stations; closing doxology: Idolaters claim a kinship (nasab) between God and the jinn; the jinn know they will be brought to judgment; The angels say: each of us has a known station; we are ranged in ranks; we glorify; When the punishment descends in their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; Whether the divine attendants (heralds [divergence between the texts]; A closing doxology and the divine title it uses [divergence between the texts]; Polemic against assigning daughters to God (the angels as females) while preferring sons for themselves; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly.

matches.label: Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring
matches.note: Divine offspring. Gen: wa-yyirʾû ḇənê-hā-ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-bənôṯ hā-ʾāḏām ... yāḇōʾû bənê hā-ʾĕlōhîm ʾel-bənôṯ hā-ʾāḏām wə-yāləḏû lāhem. 'Sons of God' exist and beget with human women. Q: a-lā innahum min ifkihim la-yaqūlūna walada llāhu wa-innahum la-kādhibūn ... wa-jaʿalū baynahu wa-bayna l-jinnati nasaban ... subḥāna llāhi ʿammā yaṣifūn. Any begetting by God, or kinship (nasab) between God and the jinn, is denied as a lie. The Quran's target is Arab 'daughters of God', but the language of divine filiation is the point of contact.

passages.text: וַיִּרְא֤וּ בְנֵי הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת בְּנ֣וֹת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֥י טֹבֹ֖ת הֵ֑נָּה וַיִּקְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נָשִׁ֔ים מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּחָֽרוּ

הַנְּפִלִ֞ים הָי֣וּ בָאָרֶץ֮ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֒ וְגַ֣ם אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבֹ֜אוּ בְּנֵ֤י הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל בְּנ֣וֹת הָֽאָדָ֔ם וְיָלְד֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם הֵ֧מָּה הַגִּבֹּרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מֵעוֹלָ֖ם אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַשֵּֽׁם
وَلَدَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
وَجَعَلُوا۟ بَيْنَهُۥ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَبًا وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ ٱلْجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ

evidence.text: No longer produced by the current pipeline (2026-10-31): its statistics or cognate checks no longer meet the thresholds after a method change. Kept for review.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The man of the fish (Dhū l-Nūn) cries from the darknesses 'There is no god but you; I was a wrongdoer' and is saved (weight 6.3); The prophet prays to God from inside the fish [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The prophet prays to God from inside the fish (weight 6.3); At God's command the fish vomits the prophet onto dry land (weight 6.3). Pair score 25.1.

Only in Lot's old woman; Jonah and the fish: The fish casts the prophet onto a barren shore while he is sick; Jonah ran away (abaqa, as a runaway slave) to the laden ship; Had Jonah not been among those who glorify God he would have stayed in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection; Jonah is sent to a hundred thousand or more; they believe and are granted enjoyment for a while; The hearers pass by the ruins of Lot's people morning and night; Nineveh has more than 120,000 people who do not know their right hand from their left; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; The city to which Jonah is sent believes and is spared [divergence between the texts]; Jonah flees by ship [divergence between the texts]; Sailors cast lots to learn on whose account the disaster has come, and the lot falls on the prophet; Sailors cast lots to learn on whose account the disaster has come, and the lot falls on the prophet [divergence between the texts]; God makes a plant (qiqayon, gourd or castor) grow overnight to shade the prophet; and 4 more.

Only in Do you have a book or oaths binding God?; the shin laid bare; the companion of the fish; the evil eye: Do not be like the companion of the fish (sahib al-hut, Jonah) who cried out while choking with grief; God leads the deniers on step by step (istidraj) from where they do not know, and grants them respite; his plan is firm; Had not grace from his Lord reached him he would have been cast onto the barren shore blameworthy; but his Lord chose him and made him righteous; On the day when the shin is laid bare (yukshafu 'an saq) and they are called to prostrate but cannot; The unbelievers almost make the prophet slip with their (evil) eyes when they hear the reminder; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; At God's command the fish vomits the prophet onto dry land [divergence between the texts]; 'Are your unbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity (bara'a) in the scriptures (zubur)?'; The prophet is bitterly angry that God has spared the sinners; The prophet is bitterly angry that God has spared the sinners [divergence between the texts]; The word of God comes to the prophet a second time with the same commission; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; and 3 more.

sides.note: In the fish. Jonah: wa-yman YHWH dāḡ gāḏôl liḇlōaʿ ʾeṯ-yônâ ... šəlōšâ yāmîm û-šəlōšâ lêlôṯ, then a full psalm (qārāʾṯî mi-ṣṣārâ lî ... mi-bbeṭen šəʾôl šiwwaʿtî). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The fire does not harm the hero (weight 6.8); Hero thrown into a fire or furnace by a king or people (weight 6.2). Pair score 13.1.

Only in Abraham and the idols in the Quran: Hero blames the largest idol for the destruction; Hero reasons from the stars, moon and sun to the one God; Hero smashes or burns idols; Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols.

Only in The golden image and the fiery furnace: God sends his angel to rescue his servants from death; All are commanded to bow to the king's image on pain of being thrown into a blazing furnace; The flames kill the men who throw the heroes into the furnace; A fourth figure appears walking in the fire, looking like a son of the gods (bar elahin); The furnace is heated seven times more than usual; The king sets up a golden image sixty cubits high and six wide on the plain of Dura; Envious courtiers 'eat the pieces' (slander) of the Jews and denounce their non-compliance to the king; The pagan king decrees that anyone who blasphemes or fails to fear the Jewish God will be punished; The rescued have not a hair singed, their garments unchanged, and no smell of fire on them; Long repeated list of imperial officials (satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates); A listed orchestra of instruments (horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, symphonia) signals the moment to bow to the idol; The faithful declare that God can save them, but even if he does not, they will not serve the king's gods; and 6 more.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָא ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ

sides.note: The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

passages.text: (6:25) וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת (6:26) וּבָנִ֨יתָ מִזְבֵּ֜חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עַ֣ל רֹ֧אשׁ הַמָּע֛וֹז הַזֶּ֖ה בַּמַּֽעֲרָכָ֑ה וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהַעֲלִ֣יתָ עוֹלָ֔ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּכְרֹֽת (6:27) וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה (6:28) וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי

וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת

וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה

leads.title: Noah in the Quran ↔ The Flood (full read)
leads.summary: 9 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 6.5); Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain (weight 6.4); Hero singled out as righteous or pious (weight 6.2); Waters pour both from the sky and from springs of the earth (weight 6.2); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 6.2); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 6.1); All others perish (weight 5.9); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Pair score 54.8.

Only in Noah in the Quran: Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; Vessel described by its planks and fastenings; The flood waters are hot or boiling; Hero's life or mission spans 950 years; A member of the hero's family is lost; A specific sign marks the moment to board; People mock the hero while he builds the vessel; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.
